digest.component_or_area: LLM gate (plan-review, code-review, completion-verification); deprecation registry; observability probe
propositions: Per-gate costs measured: plan-review $3.02/run, code-review $1.42/run, completion-verifier $2.24/run; mean $11.85/completed ticket; experiments ruled out Haiku for agentic review and Nova Pro for completion verification due to false-accepts and finding-loss.

Code-review blocking decision does not consult severity axes for 98.5% of findings (3,353 of 3,363 findings at blocking_enabled=False); the 0.95 threshold is unreachable by all-but-one finding (only 7 of 432 ordinal combinations attain it, requiring conjunction of blast_radius=system AND likelihood=high AND reversibility=hard, which occurs zero times in 3,738 graded findings).

Deprecation removal-readiness: only the retired .gitattributes migration arm (15 LOC) is genuinely expired and removable now; single-pass review surfaces and REBAR_LLM_MODEL supersession are removable only in a pre-1.0 breaking window per announce-then-remove precedent; resolved_statuses inert-key removal is approval-gated.

Five CloudWatch alarm firings 2026-08-12: three true-positive review-interrupt bound-exceeded events (deferred_for 1810/1820/1810/1930s vs bound=1800s suggest DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX undersizing), two false-positives from probe pattern-matching review-bot LLM output as observability markers, two defects filed in observability.sh (cold-start offset initialization and unanchored grep patterns).

Historical audit of per-criterion re-review carry-forward rejected: 37% of BLOCK→re-review transitions introduce new blocking criteria not in original block; same-material re-runs produce 0% all-new-criteria blocks (15% mixed = nondeterminism floor), confirming new-criteria blocks on revised material are real revision-induced defects.

Overlap-drain contributes zero findings across 2,093 plan-reviews and generates ~$165/5-days local cost plus failure storms; recommend overlap_drain=off pending redesign or restriction to ticket-creation only.
